nodes.label: pr_library table (read-only source of truth)
nodes.rationale: Zero INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE call sites were found in aigen-backend; the table is treated as immutable because SAP business rules already validated the data and the app has no control over the external ETL schedule.

nodes.label: qcf_library table (Quotation Comparison Form)
nodes.rationale: Serves as final approval stage before SAP PO, cost comparison of item_value vs vendor_price, audit trail, and the CL decision point; rfq_item_id links each QCF row back to its RFQ row.

nodes.label: php artisan prpo:download insert (iSourcing sync)
nodes.rationale: Requires a dedicated procure-prod@'%' MySQL user on task_board; reusing an existing pr_number requires deleting exports_data/item_card rows first because the sync is not idempotent.

nodes.label: POST /mock/search-library
nodes.rationale: Only one unique pr_number is allowed per bulk operation so the downstream iSourcing artisan sync maps a single PR deterministically to exports_data and item_card.

nodes.label: Phase 1: Data Creation (Mock API + iSourcing Sync)
nodes.norm_label: phase 1: data creation (mock api + isourcing sync)

nodes.label: Phase 3: Vendor Response (PUT /pr/vendor/submit_penawaran)
nodes.rationale: Vendor rejection (status_vendor 2) auto-assigns a Level 2 vendor rather than failing the RFQ, preserving competitive sourcing.

nodes.label: duplicateRFQ() - bulk Level 2 vendor reassignment
nodes.rationale: Declined Level 1 items are duplicated rather than mutated so the original vendor's decline stays on record as an audit trail while statuses are reset for the Level 2 vendor.

nodes.label: rfq_library table
nodes.rationale: Only two insertion paths exist; cron and sync jobs deliberately never insert, only read and update, keeping RFQ creation confined to the PR submission and vendor-reassignment flows.

nodes.label: Mock RFQ validation rules
nodes.rationale: Enforces status consistency (quotation_date required when status_vendor=1; status_dic cannot be 1 unless status_vendor is 1; QCF only at milestone 18 or 20) and a plus/minus 50 percent vendor price deviation cap, so generated fixtures cannot express states the real workflow could never reach.

nodes.rationale: Activates a Level 2 vendor at H+3 when only Level 1 exists, so competition is introduced before the deadline rather than after a failure.

nodes.label: H+6 Reminder (sendSixDayPendingRfqReminders)
nodes.rationale: Escalates visibility to CS (milestone 22 for vendor 1, 5 for vendor 2) instead of acting automatically, giving a human the chance to intervene before auto-escalation.

nodes.label: H+9 Auto iSourcing (handleNineDayRfqFollowUp)
nodes.rationale: Only fires when exactly two vendors exist and both are still pending, so RFQs with any vendor response are never auto-diverted to manual procurement.

nodes.label: Role-aware capability fields (canApprove, canManualSourcing)
nodes.rationale: Returning booleans rather than raw serverGroups plus clApprovedAt keeps the GEMS rule from being reimplemented in two codebases; it changes canApprove semantics from per-endpoint to per-authenticated-role.

nodes.label: CS token access to QCF detail
nodes.norm_label: cs token access to qcf detail
nodes.rationale: QCF tokens are entirely unbound - the payload carries only qcf_number/rfq_number/vendor_code and the middleware verifies signature and expiry without consulting qcf_token_email, so a revoked token still works; this answer was later reversed by planning decision 2.

nodes.label: Management QCF approval eligibility gap
nodes.rationale: The update predicate checks only qcf_number and null approval fields, so Management can approve a GEMS QCF before or after CL and trigger Auto PO; fix is 403 for policy denial and 409 for state conflicts.

nodes.label: Manual Sourcing endpoint has no role or state guard
nodes.norm_label: manual sourcing endpoint has no role or state guard
nodes.rationale: The iSourcing board mutation runs before RFQ/QCF status updates, so a late rejection would orphan a board card; validation must happen before any mutation, and the client-supplied is_system_action flag is not a security boundary.

nodes.label: Phase 3 authorization hardening
nodes.rationale: Kept ungated by the kill switch because reverting the fixes would reintroduce security holes; the broken CL ownership filter (scalar cl_id versus an expected {user_id, role} object) let any authenticated role reach CL approval logic.

nodes.label: qcfWorkflowPolicy centralized GEMS policy helper
nodes.rationale: Every predicate takes rows loaded from the database, never request-body fields, and returns {allowed, code, message} so callers can map denials to 403 versus 409; GEMS behavior was previously only a side effect of seeded configuration.

nodes.label: GET /pr/sourcing-reason
nodes.rationale: Reasons are filtered per role by joining the JWT role slug to isourcing roles.id and then config_reason.role_id, so CS and Admin see different dropdown options.

nodes.label: prosesToIsourcing() board card push
nodes.rationale: Branches on countByCardTitle: a new Kanban board card plus item_card/exports_data rows when the PR has never entered iSourcing, otherwise only the missing items are appended and presence in the main list is ensured.

nodes.rationale: Validated against business-day expiry excluding weekends, and some endpoints accept the token as a path parameter instead of an Authorization header.

nodes.label: qcf_library.sub_category_id lineage blocker
nodes.rationale: category_matrices is keyed on category_id but qcf_library has no sub_category_id column, so CS PIC resolution has no join key; the lineage qcf_library.rfq_item_id to rfq_library.id to rfq_library.sub_category_id must be materialized first.

nodes.label: buildGemsManualPoRecipients resolver
nodes.rationale: If To is empty after resolution the send is skipped and logged rather than inventing placeholder addresses; a shared normalizeEmailRecipients dedupes To/Cc case-insensitively for all callers.

nodes.label: DASHBOARD_STATUS.WAITING_MANUAL_PO mapping
nodes.rationale: The seven role-scoped label maps must stay permanent even after rollback, because rows that reached milestone 26 during the pilot still exist and would otherwise render as an unknown status; the flag gates transitions, not interpretation.

nodes.label: GEMS branch in approveByCL
nodes.rationale: Skips syncAutoPO, the Management token and the Management email; the approval transaction commits before SMTP so a failed notification returns HTTP 200 with notification.status=failed rather than rolling back a valid approval. findExpiredManagementReviewItems must exclude GEMS or the rows get swept into Management expiry processing.

nodes.label: gems-qcf-approved-manual-po email template
nodes.rationale: Must contain no approval action, Management request or Management recipient; the summary-table mapping is extracted from approval-for-quotation-summary.js into a shared partial rather than duplicated.

nodes.label: qcf_library.sub_category_id migration and backfill
nodes.rationale: Backfill runs before the FK so pre-existing orphans do not break the constraint; ON DELETE SET NULL is chosen over RESTRICT/CASCADE so deleting a category cannot block or destroy QCF history, deliberately diverging from the FK-less rfq_library precedent.

nodes.label: WAITING_MANUAL_PO milestone (26)
nodes.rationale: GEMS previously had no stable post-CL resting state because Auto PO advanced rows straight to 20; milestone 26 is terminal because the PO is keyed into SAP by hand and nothing writes po_number back, so these rows never reach 'PO Published'.

nodes.label: Mock RFQ scenario templates
nodes.rationale: Eight named templates (pending_rfq, vendor_submitted, dic_approved, cl_approved, complete_workflow, dual_vendor_pending, one_approved_one_pending, declined_scenario) fix consistent status_vendor/status_dic/status_milestone triples so testers do not hand-assemble invalid state.

nodes.label: GEMS_MANUAL_PO_FLOW kill switch
nodes.rationale: A single env var was chosen over config_autopo (read by the external import-pr cron, unverifiable risk) and over a feature_flags table (too much machinery for a one-month pilot); it fails closed, is read at approval time not snapshotted, and must be set in both the app and cron environments or the halves disagree silently.

nodes.label: In-flight GEMS QCF backlog stranding risk
nodes.norm_label: in-flight gems qcf backlog stranding risk
nodes.rationale: 8 GEMS rows sit at milestone 18 awaiting Management; once Management is blocked nobody can move them because CL cannot re-approve and the new path only fires at approval time. Mitigation: deploy with the flag off, let Management drain the backlog, verify the count is zero, then flip the flag - no data migration needed.
